note: CoALA (Sumers et al., TMLR): language agents framed as modular memory (incl. procedural), structured action space, generalized decision cycle — the cognitive-architecture backbone of the hybrid.
LLM-Modulo (Kambhampati et al., ICML 2024): LLMs generate, external sound validators guarantee correctness — the pattern behind skills_draft + validator + bind.

Voyager: LLM-authored, compositional skill library compounds competence (3.3x unique items, up to 15.3x faster milestones) and transfers to a new Minecraft world — evidence for the library layer and per-game data portability.

SwiftSage (NeurIPS 2023 spotlight): fast policy for routine steps, LLM invoked only on hard states; significantly outperforms SayCan, ReAct, Reflexion — fast/slow layering beats single-layer prompting.

DPT-Agent (ACL 2025 main): FSM/code-as-policy system 1 under LLM system 2 for real-time simultaneous human-AI collaboration; experiments show System 1 or System 2 alone is insufficient — the direct empirical case for composition.

KRAFTON PUBG Ally (NVIDIA ACE): shipped dual-system co-op teammate — on-device 2B SLM decision core over a behavior tree at game tick rate; 'reflex-level actions never have to wait for the model'; boundary between layers was the hard engineering.

Mindcraft modes.js: open-source existence proof of a priority-ordered reflex layer with interrupts running every tick under the LLM action loop; interrupted actions return to the LLM as auto-messages.
Mindcraft README: LLM-written skills (newAction) exist but are gated behind allow_insecure_coding, off by default — the cautionary pattern my validated-declarative-skills default avoids.

Brooks' subsumption architecture: layered reactive control, 'the world is its own best model' (the ancestor of adapter-side until conditions), with the known weakness (no deliberation) that system 2 exists to patch.

Survey on LLM-based game agents: unified reference architecture (memory, reasoning, perception-action interfaces); links game genres to dominant demands from low-latency control to open-ended goal formation — supports per-timescale ownership.

LLM inference latency numbers (round 1): TTFT ~200-500 ms well-tuned (multi-second on long contexts), 10-50 ms per output token; a 500-token response takes over 15 seconds at 300 ms TTFT + 30 ms/token — grounds the attack on the pure-tool-calling baseline's post-interrupt idle gap.

SIMA 2 announcement (round 2): zero-shot success on untrained games (ASKA, MineDojo), concept transfer across games, Genie-3-world play — but a limited research preview for a small cohort, no API or weights; grounds both the concession to advocate-model and the availability counterattack.
